- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model consistently overpredicts in the first 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; apply early correction by 1–2% downward.
- After a price spike (e.g., >79.0), model often overreacts with a sustained upward bias; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or use mean-reversion anchor.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model shows persistent lag; add 1–2% lag correction to align with true momentum.
- Model underperforms in the final 5–7 days of horizon when sentiment is positive; increase forecast slightly to avoid premature mean reversion.
- When sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., +0.67 → -0.67 → +0.67), model fails to adjust; apply sentiment-weighted smoothing to forecast.
